sessĭto , āvi, 1,
I.v. freq. n. [id.], to sit much or long (very rare): quam deam (Suadam) in Pericli labris scripsit Eupolis sessitavisse, * Cic. Brut. 15, 59: “sessitandi regio,” of the seat, of the posteriors, App. Dogm. Plat. 1, p. 10, 40 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
